title: Frontend: Guess the number
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Guess the number. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Export App({secret=42}). Controlled Guess input accepts integers 1..100. Guess button reports Too low, Too high, Correct, or Invalid guess in [data-testid="feedback"]. A correct round ignores later guesses until Restart, which clears input/feedback. Secret is injected for deterministic tests.
constraints: Export default App. Only react and react/jsx-runtime imports are supported. The DOM contract and supplied props define the exercise.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Create the secret at round initialization rather than on every render.
alternativeApproaches: Add a reproducible seed and a history view without leaking the secret into normal UI state displays.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Bounds; non-integer input; repeat guess.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
